issues.legal_issue: An unequivocal statement made by retained counsel on a matter within the subject of the representation binds the client when the counsel did not exceed the authority conferred.
material_facts: The landlord appealed from orders arising out of a tenant’s eviction proceeding.
Counsel retained to represent the landlord in the eviction proceeding unequivocally stated before the High Court that the tenant would be re-inducted in equivalent space after reconstruction.
The landlord later asserted that counsel had made the statement without instructions, but did not claim that he had expressly instructed counsel not to make it.
The statement concerned the subject matter of the proceeding, and the landlord continued to explore a possible arrangement during the appeals.
issues.conclusion: The landlord was bound by counsel’s unequivocal statement and could not resile from the re-induction commitment; the High Court was right to dismiss the review petition.
issues.legal_principle: Himalayan Coop. Group Housing Society v. Balwan Singh, (2015) 7 SCC 373, explains that counsel generally must follow the client’s instructions and ordinarily needs specific authority to compromise or surrender substantial rights; however, unequivocal admissions of fact may bind a client when they are within the authority of the representation and the lawyer has not exceeded that authority. The Court distinguished that case on these facts. It also relied on Tamil Nadu Electricity Board v. Raju Reddiar, (1997) 9 SCC 736, in observing that review petitions of this kind should not be encouraged.

rule.if: appeal_from_eviction_proceeding and counsel_retained_for_subject_matter and unequivocal_commitment_on_subject_matter and not express_instruction_against_commitment

predicates.appeal_from_eviction_proceeding: The matter was an appeal arising from a proceeding seeking a tenant’s eviction.
predicates.counsel_retained_for_subject_matter: The client had retained the lawyer to represent the client in the proceeding concerning the property.
predicates.unequivocal_commitment_on_subject_matter: The lawyer made an unequivocal commitment concerning the subject matter of the proceeding.
predicates.express_instruction_against_commitment: The client expressly instructed the lawyer not to make the commitment.

issues.definition: When an eviction appeal concerns a matter for which counsel was retained, counsel makes an unequivocal commitment on that matter, and the client did not expressly forbid it, the client is bound by the commitment.

issues.legal_issue: A court may modify the terms for a tenant’s re-induction to accommodate physical constraints while preserving a usable space and compensating for area lost, thereby implementing the landlord’s binding commitment.
material_facts: The matter was an appeal arising from an eviction proceeding in which the landlord had committed to re-induct the tenant in equivalent space after reconstruction.
The newly constructed building’s internal staircase occupied part of the ground floor and obstructed access to the upper floors unless a passage through the ground-floor premises was provided.
The landlord offered a smaller ground-floor space with a passage, and the tenant rejected it as too small and unsuitable for the tenant’s business.

The Court found that the full original area could not be provided while also accommodating access to the upper floors, but that the front portion could be separated from the rear portion, with upper-floor access provided from the rear.
The High Court had ordered daily damages for delayed re-induction, and the Supreme Court considered the area loss and the utility of the space in settling the terms of re-induction.
issues.conclusion: The Court modified the decree to require the landlord to provide the tenant the usable front portion of the ground floor, separate it from the rear portion by a wall, provide upper-floor access from the rear, and pay compensation for the area lost. The compensation replaced the High Court’s daily damages for delayed re-induction. The Court also restrained use of the upper floors until possession and compensation were delivered, appointed a receiver to oversee compliance, and directed that rent be determined by the Rent Controller after both sides had an opportunity to be heard.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied a fact-specific equitable approach to give effect to the landlord’s binding re-induction commitment, minimize the tenant’s loss of usable space, preserve the non-residential utility of the premises, and compensate for the area that could not be provided. It cited no separate statutory provision or earlier case as the basis for this remedial arrangement.

rule.if: appeal_from_eviction_proceeding and binding_reinduction_commitment and building_constraints_prevent_full_original_space and proposed_reduced_space_unusable and alternative_usable_space_available

predicates.appeal_from_eviction_proceeding: The matter was an appeal arising from a proceeding seeking a tenant’s eviction.
predicates.binding_reinduction_commitment: The landlord had made a commitment to re-induct the tenant after reconstruction.
predicates.building_constraints_prevent_full_origin: The layout of the reconstructed building prevented the landlord from providing the entire original area while maintaining access to the upper floors.
predicates.proposed_reduced_space_unusable: The tenant rejected the offered smaller space because it would not be usable for the tenant’s business.
predicates.alternative_usable_space_available: The court found that a different portion could be provided in a way that remained usable and allowed separate access to the upper floors.

issues.definition: When an eviction appeal involves a binding re-induction commitment, building constraints prevent delivery of the full original space, the offered reduced space is unusable, and an alternative usable space is available, the court may order that space and compensation for the area lost.
